title: fluorostats: deterministic, CPU-only quantification of fluorescence microscopy
description:
fluorostats is an open-source Python library and command-line tool for quantifying fluorescence microscopy images and volumes. Every metric is a deterministic, training-free, CPU-only function of its inputs: repeated runs return identical bits, and no step holds a learned weight or draws a random seed.

The library spans 2D coverage and 3D volume fraction, connectivity and topology (Euler number, connected components), skeleton and vascular network metrics, per-object morphometry, annular/tube morphometry, network organisation, spatial heterogeneity, depth-resolved viability, and 3D rendering. It integrates a statistics layer that general imaging platforms omit, including non-parametric tests with effect sizes, stratified and interaction tests, Benjamini-Hochberg multiplicity control, bootstrap confidence intervals, agreement statistics and bootstrap power analysis, so that quantification and inference never leave the same pipeline.

Every metric, and the scoring code used to benchmark it, is validated against a canonical reference implementation or against analytic ground truth. This deposit is the exact version used in the accompanying manuscript, and includes the full benchmark harness; continuous integration tests the package on Python 3.10-3.13 and at its declared minimum dependency versions.

The derived metric tables behind the benchmark figures are bundled at benchmarks/results/, each with a record of the code commit and parameters that produced it. Figures 3, 5, S1, S3, S4 and S5 regenerate from these tables alone, and so does Figure 6 except panel (c), whose two micrographs render laboratory stacks that are not deposited; Figures 2, 4 and S2 also read public datasets, whose licences, URLs and expected folder layout are listed in benchmarks/DATA_MANIFEST.md. Raw microscopy is not included, except two 400 x 400 display crops of CC-BY-4.0 VesselExpress data (benchmarks/results/ve_crops.npz), which a bundled producer rebuilds from the public volumes.
